newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cognac sales still falling in Japan - Remy.
newsitem.headline: Cognac sales still falling in Japan - Remy.

text.p: Cognac sales in Japan are still falling this year but a slide in cognac sales in China appears to have halted at mid-year, Remy-Cointreau Managing Director Marc Heriard Dubreuil said on Tuesday.

"The Japanese market, which was for years the most profitable, is in decline and the decline continues," he told a news conference. He said cognac sales in Japan were down around seven or eight percent since the beginning of 1996 due to a slump in lavish business spending.
However, he added: "We consider the drop in the Chinese market has stopped".
Dubreuil said Remy was stronger in China than the competition, while the Hennessy cognac brand, owned by the LVMH group, was the leader in Japan.
Remy generates 57 percent of its cognac sales in Asia, 21 percent in Europe, 20 percent in America and two percent elsewhere.
Its first-half cognac sales totalled 941 million francs -- 351 million in the first quarter and 590 million in the second -- down two percent from year-earlier levels.
Remy's sales for the six months to September 30 totalled 3.07 billion francs.
Dubreuil said cognac sales were strong in the United States, the biggest market, but weak in Europe.
He said the spending climate in Europe was not conducive to sales of expensive spirits and "sales were stable or slightly lower", but the company would maintain its price policy.

In its other sectors, liquor, wine and spirits sales rose four percent to one billion francs, helped by a 13 percent rise in Cointreau sales. Champagne sales were steady at 343 million francs, and sales of wines and spirits made by other companies but distributed by Remy rose 16 percent to 781 million francs.
The company said U.S. publicity about the health benefits of red wine helped boost wine sales in Asia.
It reported good sales of Famous Grouse and Macallan whiskies, Tequila Tres Magueyes and Italian Antinori wines.
Remy this year launched "the first champagne for women" under the brand Princesse. Officials said it was now available at retailers and supermarkets but gave little indication of its performance.
